code_quality.description: Subtract function is absent from the diff. The spec requires adding `Subtract(a, b int) int` to calc/calc.go. The calc/ directory appears as `?? calc/` in git status — untracked and unchanged.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add `func Subtract(a, b int) int { return a - b }` to calc/calc.go and commit the file.

code_quality.description: Tests for Subtract are absent. The spec requires tests covering Subtract(5,3)==2, Subtract(0,0)==0, and Subtract(3,5)==-2 in calc/calc_test.go. No changes to this file appear in the diff.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add table-driven or individual test cases for all three acceptance criteria to calc/calc_test.go.

code_quality.description: effectiveStatus diverges from FinalizeStage.Run. effectiveStatus requires allDone (every task.Status == "done") AND all three gates to return ready_for_review, but FinalizeStage was simplified in this diff to check only the three gates. A run with a failed task from an earlier cycle but all gates passing will be finalized as ready_for_review by FinalizeStage yet show needs_human in every evidence file written by EvidenceStage.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Remove the allDone loop from effectiveStatus and mirror FinalizeStage's logic: return ready_for_review when FinalValidationPassed && FinalReviewPassed && FinalAcceptancePassed, regardless of individual task statuses.

code_quality.description: maxTaskID in plan.go duplicates maxTaskIDInQueue in taskloop.go. Both parse t-NNN suffixes; any format change must be made in two places.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Extract a shared parseTaskIDNum helper into the specloop package and call it from both sites.

code_quality.description: The baseline capture call to DetectFilesChanged silently discards its error with //nolint:errcheck. If the call fails the baseline is never captured; the second (delta) call will also treat itself as a baseline capture (since baseline remains nil), silently returning empty and missing all file changes for that task.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Return the error from the baseline call or, if baseline capture fails, mark the detector as disabled for this task iteration and fall back to runner-reported FilesChanged.

code_quality.description: hashAllFiles always returns a nil error — every error path inside the function handles the failure locally and continues. The caller's `if err != nil` branch is dead code, and the error return type on the function signature is misleading.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Change the signature to `func hashAllFiles(absDir string) map[string]string` and remove the dead error check at the call site.

code_quality.description: filterForbiddenFixTasks detects the test-file constraint by matching natural-language substrings ("test file", "do not modify", "must not be modified"). This will miss paraphrases, false-positive on unrelated text, and silently fail to enforce other constraint types despite the generic function name.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either scope the function name to its actual behaviour (filterTestFileTasks) or replace substring matching with a structured constraint representation populated during CompileStage.

code_quality.description: The stateful two-call semantics of the GitFilesChanged closure (first call captures baseline, second call returns delta, then resets) are non-obvious. Any caller that adds an extra invocation or skips one silently corrupts state; the taskloop already uses //nolint:errcheck to suppress baseline calls, signalling that the interface is awkward.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Consider splitting into two explicit methods — Snapshot() and Delta() — or pass a context/token from the first call to the second to make the pairing explicit and detectable at compile time.

spec_alignment.description: The diff replaces the entire CONTINUE.md (1506 lines added) with content unrelated to the add-subtract spec. While this file is internal project state and not part of the spec deliverables, the replacement wipes the prior worktree context without completing the actual in-scope work.

spec_alignment.description: `effectiveStatus` checks both task statuses (allDone loop) AND the three gate booleans to determine ready_for_review, but `FinalizeStage.Run` was simplified in this diff to check only the three gates (removing the allDone requirement). A run with failed tasks from earlier cycles that passes all three gates will be finalized as ready_for_review by FinalizeStage, but effectiveStatus will return needs_human — causing review.md and summary.md to disagree with the actual final status.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Remove the allDone check from effectiveStatus to match FinalizeStage's gate-only logic: `if rs.FinalValidationPassed && rs.FinalReviewPassed && rs.FinalAcceptancePassed { return ready_for_review }`.

spec_alignment.description: Error from the DetectFilesChanged baseline call is silently suppressed with `//nolint:errcheck`. If the baseline capture fails, the subsequent delta call will compare against a nil map, potentially reporting spurious file changes or missing real ones.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Log or propagate the baseline error rather than silencing it; at minimum fall back to the runner's own FilesChanged on baseline failure.

spec_alignment.description: `maxTaskID(tasks []runstore.Task)` in plan.go and `maxTaskIDInQueue(queue []taskEntry)` in taskloop.go implement identical t-NNN parsing logic. This duplication will diverge silently if the ID format changes.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Extract a shared `parseTaskIDNum(id string) (int, bool)` helper in the specloop package and call it from both sites.

spec_alignment.description: `filterForbiddenFixTasks` detects test-file constraints by matching natural-language substrings ("test file", "do not modify", "must not be modified"). This heuristic will miss paraphrases and false-positive on unrelated constraint text. The function is also only invoked for this one constraint pattern despite its generic name.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Either scope the function name to `filterForbiddenTestFileTasks` to make the heuristic's limited scope explicit, or replace the string-matching with a structured constraint representation populated at compile time.

spec_alignment.description: The stateful two-call semantics of the GitFilesChanged closure (first call = capture baseline, second call = compute delta, then reset) are non-obvious and fragile. Any call-site change that adds an extra invocation or skips one will silently corrupt the state. The taskloop already uses `//nolint:errcheck` comments to suppress baseline calls, indicating the interface is awkward.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Consider splitting into explicit `Snapshot()` and `Delta(snapshot)` calls, or wrapping the closure in a named type with `Before()` and `After()` methods to make the two-phase protocol visible at the call site.
